description: A finance director must authorize and structure an employee share-repurchase tender program, setting the offer size, price, cash budget, tax handling, eligibility rules, and safeguards with input from human resources, treasury, legal, and tax.

shared_context.S1: The company has 1,200,000 outstanding employee-held common shares and is considering a voluntary company repurchase program.
shared_context.S2: The board has approved developing the program, but has not approved its final operating terms.
shared_context.S3: The company's current common-share valuation for internal planning is $23.50 per share.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding finance decision, and company practice is for finance to conduct a final review with treasury, tax, legal, and human resources before issuing program terms.

PF1.text: While reviewing the draft tender documents this week, Ravi confirmed that the program must screen participants for material nonpublic information and use an independent tender administrator; these safeguards are not yet in the draft.

PF2.text: Marta confirmed in this morning's twelve-week cash forecast that the program can spend no more than $4,230,000 without breaching the approved liquidity buffer, so the final terms must cap cash consideration at exactly that amount.

PF3.text: Jonah received a tax memorandum yesterday confirming that repurchase proceeds must be withheld at exactly 22% and remitted within three business days; the memorandum has not yet been added to the finance approval packet.

PF4.text: Leah confirmed from the equity plan records this week that only employees with at least 12 months of service may participate, and any oversubscription must be allocated pro rata rather than by first-come priority; HR has not yet updated the draft enrollment rules.

acceptance_conditions: The program must be authorized for a maximum repurchase of 180,000 shares at $23.50 per share.
Cash consideration must be capped at exactly $4,230,000.
Repurchase proceeds must have exactly 22% withheld and be remitted within three business days.
Only employees with at least 12 months of service may participate, and oversubscription must be allocated pro rata.
The enrollment process must screen for material nonpublic information and use an independent tender administrator.

decisive_facts.why: The board-approved concept has no stated safeguards; PF1 changes mnpi_screen_required and independent_tender_administrator from false or unspecified to true.
The planning valuation supports a broad share count, but PF2 changes the maximum repurchase to exactly 180,000 shares and the cash_consideration_cap_usd to exactly $4,230,000.
No tax treatment appears in the draft program; PF3 changes withholding_rate_pct to exactly 22, tax_remittance_within_days to exactly 3, and requires the tax_remittance commitment.
The draft has no enrollment allocation rule; PF4 changes minimum_service_months to exactly 12, turns on pro_rata_oversubscription_allocation, and requires the pro_rata_allocation commitment.
